courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: Let's now create some custom CSS style and I'll do that on that offers page where I'm not super
happy with the styles I currently have there.
Now of course, you can also change that with the default tools Inoic gives you, for example on the discover
page,
we also have a nice looking list with just the default Ionic features of using a h2 tag and a paragraph
tag giving us this list which looks really nice in my opinion but I want to have a different style here
and I also want to show you how to write your own CSS or Sass rules and how they fit into the big
picture.
So therefore let's have a look at our offers page here,
here it is
and there we have these ion-items where I currently only have that label with the h1 tag.
I will now generate a new component which simply holds the content that will be rendered inside of
an ion-item,
so basically this part here where I will then use custom CSS rules to adjust the styling.
Now you can of course create that component manually,
I'll use Ionic generate component here and I want to generate that component in my places folder, then
under offers and then offer-item, of course you can name your component however you want. I'll grab
that thumbnail and that ion-label content,
so basically what I had in my ion-item here or actually let's grab the entire ion-item and in the offer
item, I'll place that in here.
Now of course, we'll need to get that offer as an input to this component,
so let's quickly add @input here, offer which for now is of type place actually
and therefore you should import your place module up there as well.
Now we can access things like the imageUrl again,
so this should now work
and I want to focus on the styling now. For this, I will have my h1 tag here inside of that label
let's say
but below that, I'll add a div and in that div, I want to have a fromTo date,
so basically for which timespan am I offering this place? For that, I'll add an ion-icon here with a name
of calendar and next to that, I'll use ion-text, give this a color of primary,
so actually not my own custom CSS style here but this ion-text element which is great if we just
want to give some text a color
and here I'll put dynamic value and for now, we don't have any dates for our places or offers.
So here, I'll just call a function, getDummyDate which we'll replace later and I'll use the date pipe Angular
gives me by default which transforms this to look nice and getDummyDate is simply a function I'll
add here where I'll return new date, so which is simply the current timestamp. So with that, I got this and
I will also then add a span with the word to and then repeat that, have that calendar icon again and
get another dummy date which will technically be the same as the first one because it's still today but
again, we'll replace this with better data later.
Now let's say use this offer item here, so in my ion-item-sliding component here, I'll add app offer
item and I'll pass in my offer which here is the offer I'm looping through,
so this offer here on the right side of the equal sign refers to this offer variable, offer here in
the square brackets refers to my offer property in there and of course, also make sure that your offer
item component is declared here next to the offers page in my case. So with that if we save this, let's
have a look at our application and login and go to the offers
and this is how it looks like. Now
it's not the finished style obviously but it's getting there.
Now there are things I want to fix and that is where custom CSS code will come into play.
First of all, I have that div where I have all that information about the starting date and ending date
and I'll give this is a class of offer details and of course, you can use any name you want.
Now I'll select offer details here with a class selector and set this to use the flexbox specification
by using display flex, the default then is then the items I laid out in a row
and I want to align items vertically and center them there which we can do with align items center
and I'll quickly go to the auth service to set isAuthenticated to true again
so that when the page reloads,
we actually go back to the offer page immediately and we don't have to wait for that login animation.
So let's now have a look at what this gives us.
As this reloads, I need to login one more time but thereafter, we should be done and now this is at
least vertically centered.
Now obviously there is no spacing between the different items and to achieve spacing, we could of course
use justify content space between here but on larger displays, this will probably not look that good.
So instead, this is also something which I can achieve here in my HTML code, if we want to have some
spacing around the items, we can add some padding horizontal because I want to have spacing to the
left or right or margin horizontal here to ion-text, also to to
and to this ion-text here.
Let's see what that gives us, here I'm using these CSS utility attributes and that looks better but
it's of course way too much,
so this is not really what I want.
So let's revert this
and again it's something where custom CSS styles can save us.
I simply want to style all my items here in offer details, instead I could add a space left class selector
here and give that a margin to left of let's say five pixels.
Now space left is a class we can now assign in here, for example to this ion-text here,
space left and to all the other items there as well,
so to to here, to the calendar icon here and to this text and obviously, there would be other ways of achieving
the same look but I want to show how to write custom CSS code and this looks now nicer.
Now I also want to color the icon here and for that, we can
again, we could use custom CSS rules but I can again just use the color attribute which
ion-icon does support and there for example, set this to secondary, so let's do that for both ion-icons
here. And now if we save that, we'll have a nicely
colored icon using our secondary color
and I think the tertiary color is a bit better here by the way but that of course depends on which colors
you chose for your theme.
Last but not least, I want to style the h1 tag here and I think we can actually make this look better
if we use primary here on the icon and on ion-text here where I previously used
primary, I use tertiary which in my case here is that darker purple,
obviously it depends on the colors you chose, which style you want to implement here.
Yes,
so I'm happy with that style,
obviously you can play around with that, choose a different style,
now what about that h1 tag though?
Here again, I want to write a custom CSS rule, so in my CSS or my Sass file here, I'll select the
h1 element and by the way, Angular scopes these styles to this component,
so this h1 selector will only select h1 elements in this component here and nowhere else and
I will therefore select this h1 element and I'll reduce the font-size here to let's say 18 pixels
and give this as a border of one pixel solid and then I'll consume my global CSS variable which is available
here because in variables, we did define them in the root selector, which means they're defined
on the topmost element which is the HTML element and thanks to CSS inheritance, we can then use
them anywhere, even in this component and in this h1 tag somewhere in our component.
So here, I will use my ion-color primary variable again and I'll add some padding here of let's say eight
pixels.
Now I'll save this and see what this gives me
and that is going in the right direction,
I'll now also add a border radius of five pixels and set a text color which also is using that primary
CSS variables,
I'll just copy that code from up here and with that, we should have a nicely styled offer item here, yes,
doesn't look too bad. Now obviously, adjust this to your requirements or to your preferences.
I'm happy with this
and the most important thing is this shows how you can set your own CSS styles and how they fit in
the big picture, how you can use global CSS variables in there and how you can also combine them
with things like the color attributes to then still use some default behaviors of building components
and obviously, you can still swipe them and so on,
so this is not touched by the fact that we're using our own CSS styles here.
